record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: From escape measurements in a billiard system, what information can be recovered about the billiard dynamics, and can escape data determine or reveal the shape of the underlying billiard domain in an analogue of asking whether one can hear the shape of a drum?

evidence.quote: Finally, a question posed in [15] but for which a systematic solution does not appear to exist in the literature:
Open problem 19. Inverse problems: What information can be extracted about the dynamics of a billiard from escape measurements? Can you “peep” the shape of a drum?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded domain with piecewise smooth boundary, and let one or more "holes" $H_i \subset \partial\Omega$ (or $H_i \subset \Omega$) be designated as escape regions. Consider the billiard flow on $\Omega$: a point particle moves in straight lines at unit speed inside $\Omega$, reflecting specularly at $\partial\Omega \setminus \bigcup_i H_i$, and is removed from the system upon hitting any $H_i$. For an initial probability measure $\mu_0$ on the phase space (e.g.\ Liouville measure on the unit tangent bundle of $\Omega$), define the survival probability
$$P(t) = \mu_0\bigl(\{(x,v) : \text{the trajectory starting at } (x,v) \text{ has not entered any hole by time } t\}\bigr),$$
and, when the limit exists, the escape rate $\gamma = -\lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{1}{t}\log P(t)$. More generally, "escape measurements" may include the full function $P(t)$, distributions of escape times, hitting distributions on the holes, and analogous quantities under varying choices of holes.

The problem is the following inverse question:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] What dynamical invariants of the billiard flow on $\Omega$ (topological entropy, Lyapunov exponents, dimension spectra, periodic orbit data, the SRB measure, etc.) can be reconstructed from escape measurements?
\item[(b)] Do escape measurements (taken, if necessary, over all admissible choices of holes) determine the geometric shape of the domain $\Omega$ up to isometry, in analogy with Kac's question "Can one hear the shape of a drum?" Equivalently, do there exist non-isometric domains $\Omega_1, \Omega_2$ producing identical escape data?
\end{enumerate}

Provide a systematic theory answering (a) and (b), or exhibit explicit obstructions and counterexamples.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the survey on open billiards, which explicitly states that a systematic solution does not appear in the literature. A web search returned no subsequent works providing a general inverse theory recovering billiard shape or dynamics from escape measurements; related work addresses only the classical spectral Kac problem and isolated escape-rate computations. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hearing the shape of a drum - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Kac's question of whether the shape of a domain can be determined from spectral data; closed-system analogue of the problem in question.
status_evidence.claim: The classical analogue (Kac's problem) is well known but concerns Laplace eigenvalues rather than billiard escape measurements.
